new.analysis:
The main issue is that the whole Sep 21 – 27 plan was skipped, not that any session went wrong. The planned runs on Mon, Wed and Sat did not happen, and the four rest days were kept, so nothing was overrun. Your check-in gives no reason, and sleep (7.5 hours), stress and body check all read fine.

The week before, Sep 14 – 20, all three runs were finished, with effort between 6 and 7 out of 10 and no pain. That is the most recent week you have fully completed, so it is the safe place to restart rather than the longer week that was planned for Sep 21 – 27.

Rebuilding after a skipped week means repeating, not climbing. The 27-minute Saturday has been planned twice and never finished, so it waits until the three runs happen again.

A 5K without walking means around 40 minutes of continuous running, and your longest run so far is 2.78 km. The run blocks in this plan add up to about 42 minutes, but they are split into short pieces, so the blocks have to lengthen over the next five weeks. That only works if the runs happen, which is why consistency matters more than speed right now.

There is no hard session in this plan, because the run blocks are already the work you need. Keep every block easy, with heart rate under 145. Your averages on these runs have been 133 to 139, so that ceiling leaves room without pushing.
